title: Bankside Residences
html:
Role – Principal Designer BR

Commencement date – January 2025. Gateway 2 submission Q3 2026.

Project type – New build student accommodation three HRB blocks connected via a podium.

Taking the place of the existing Bankside House student accommodation building located behind Tate Modern, the design is developed around the idea of three ‘houses’. The accommodation will target a provision of up to 2,000-beds, grouped into three communities of around 650 students, housed in individual buildings. The three ‘houses’ are connected at the lower floors and via garden terraces.

The creation of three blocks and the distribution of social and amenity space within each building aims to break down student numbers into manageable clusters, helping the formation of communities and providing a ‘sense of home’ in each.

With one front door ‘welcoming all’, orientated towards both the LSE campus and Tate Modern, the design strengthens the connections between key institutions whilst leaning on a ‘living room’ entrance concept and creating an environment that prioritises a positive living experience with comfort and convenience.

title: Tustin Estate Phase 2
html:
Role – Principal Designer BR

Commencement date – March 2025. Gateway 2 submission Q4 2025.

Project type –  Tustin Estate New build residential consisting of two HRB’s and two non-HRB blocks.

This phase will bring 295 high-quality new homes to the eastern part of the estate, featuring a blend of thoughtfully designed maisonettes and one, two, and three-bedroom flats across four buildings. This development will not only enhance the estate’s physical landscape but also foster a thriving community spirit that resonates throughout and beyond the regeneration process.

Building on the successful community partnerships established during Phase One, Bouygues UK continues to work in close collaboration with residents to co-create their future neighbourhood.

The ambitious regeneration extends far beyond new housing. When completed, the four-phase masterplan will feature a vibrant central park, comprehensive refurbishment of existing council homes, over 1,800 sqm of commercial space, and a complete replacement primary school.

title: Belgrave House
html:
Role – Principal Designer BR

Commencement date – July 2025.

Project type – Commercial refurbishment.

Belgrave House is progressing into the next phase of redevelopment. The project will deliver a comprehensive upgrade to building services and amenity areas, starting with the reconfiguration and replacement of central plant, including new ASHPs at roof level, AHUs, and on-floor plant rooms across Levels 3–5. These floors will be brought to shell and floor condition, incorporating new louvres to the north and south façades.

The scope also includes refurbishment of lower-level areas, such as lifts, lobbies, toilets, reception, and end-of-trip facilities, alongside the replacement of the goods lift and two firefighting lifts, with passenger lifts overhauled and refurbished. Additional enhancements feature new staircases linking key levels, and the creation of a dedicated cycle entrance with lift and stair access, replacing the existing car lift.

These works will significantly improve building performance, user experience, and sustainability credentials, aligning the asset with modern workplace standards.

title: Tribeca Phase 2
html:
Role – Principal Designer BR

Commencement date – April 2025.

Project type – Two new build office and lab spaces with 69 residential units.

Tribeca is a major life sciences development in the heart of King’s Cross. Delivering over 400,000 sqft of new buildings across four plots, including state-of-the-art laboratory and office space, 69 residential apartments, retail units, and a new public realm.

Located within London’s Knowledge Quarter, the scheme sits between Regent’s Canal and St Pancras Way, just a short walk from the Francis Crick Institute. The project will transform a former industrial site into a high-performance campus designed for scientific research, commercial innovation and urban living.

Key sustainability achievements include:

  • BREEAM Outstanding, WELL Platinum, WiredScore Platinum
  • Net zero carbon in operation, using all-electric systems and 100% renewable energy
  • Low-carbon materials, including London’s first commercial use of unfired earth bricks
  • Resilient lab-ready buildings, designed for flexibility and future tenant fit-outs

title: Astor House
html:
Role – Principal Designers Advisor – BR and CDM

Commencement date – June 2024. Gateway 2 submission Q3 2025.

Project type – Re-cladding and fire safety upgrades to two HRB’s and one non-HRB student accommodation blocks.

Blocks A & B and the Studio Block will undergo a major upgrade to improve fire safety, façade performance, and durability. Works include installing a new sprinkler system with plant and tanks, replacing selected cladding and feature box framing, and re-rendering sections. Fire protection will be strengthened through cavity barrier installation and upgrades to spandrel panels, including replacing combustible insulation. Additional remedial works will address perimeter steel beams and edge-of-slab details.

The Studio Block will also receive cavity barriers to zinc cladding and stone wall tops, spandrel panel upgrades, and feature framing replacements. These improvements ensure compliance with modern standards, enhance building resilience, and deliver a refreshed, cohesive appearance. The programme is designed to minimise disruption for residents while safeguarding long-term asset value and aligning the development with current safety regulations.

The Solution

A Partnership Built on Understanding

Green Hat’s team collaborates closely with J2R, aligning with their goals to foster continuous improvement. For businesses seeking proactive, collaborative, and helpful support, Green Hat is a valuable partner in growth and workplace safety.

title: HMP Swansea Prison Security Building
html:
RIBA Stages: 

  • RIBA Stage 4: Technical Design
  • RIBA Stage 5: Construction
  • RIBA Stage 6: Handover and Closeout

Practical Commencement: Spring 2024

Project Type

Refurbishment to Grade II listed security building, full refurbishment including structural alterations and M&E refit.

Points to Note:

Works will be carried out in a live prison environment creates a number of additional challenges.  The vaulted ceiling on the first floor is collapsing, confined space works to the roof wings either side of the vaulted ceiling.

This refurbishment is expected to be intensive including the removal of existing internal walls, renewing rewiring (power and lights), upgrade of toilets and kitchenettes. Redecoration and replacing floor coverings throughout.

How the Contract will be Delivered Successfully:

Although the project is not due to commence on site until the Spring of 2024, Green Hat are in continuous liaison and discussions with the client during the pre-construction phase not only on design and phasing of works but also to address potential security concerns, potential disruptions to daily operations and the need to ensure the safety and security of inmates, staff, and construction personnel. It is essential that the refurbishment project proceeds smoothly whilst while maintaining the operational integrity of the jail facilities.

They are people you can talk to on a practical level and most of all trust. Their approach to timely expert delivery makes them the premier ‘go to’ organisation for a fast, thorough and compliant service.”

Howard Davies – ISG Ltd
